_doc: OLDENKOTT dating cabinet (#52, WAVE F — THE ARCHIVE-BORN CABINET, built 2026-07-17-eve). The Rhenish tobacco dynasty's pipe brand. ★OUR OWN HARVEST ANTEDATES THE LITERATURE: pipedia says the German company 'produced pipes starting in 1932', but our Europeana-fulltext snippet-verified BERLIN CAMPAIGN (May-June 1926, 8 issues: '…geraucht aus einer eleganten Original-Oldenkott-Pfeife') proves Oldenkott-BRANDED pipes in commerce by 1926 -> wordmark floor 1926 encoded (maker attribution for 1926-32 open). SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Oldenkott.json (detailed; internal contradictions flagged) + our oldenkott_dating facts (ANNO graded: 1863='fiction' novel; Kruger 1901; firm style 1918) + eu_ft grading + Europeana museum artifacts (23). CONFLICTS noted: closure 1992 (main text, Kersten era) vs 'factory in Hallen closed April 1982, workers to VAUEN' (Lopes paragraph) — encoded wide w/ both; founding 1740 (infobox) vs 1760 Amsterdam (text).

history_anchors._doc: Tobacco dynasty: 1740/1760 origins (Henricus Oldenkott/Rees + Hermannus Oldenkott/Ahaus lines; Amsterdam house — 'Herms, Oldenkott und Zonen in Ahaus mit einem Zweiggeschäft in Amsterdam' in 1918 print, our ANNO grade). 1838 August Kersten (Rees) buys Heinric Oldenkott factories (Elten + Weesp). One of Germany's largest tobacco firms (Kruger smoked Oldenkott Knaster in exile; his likeness on packets — 1901, our ANNO grade; our eu_ft mass = the Dutch 1850s-70s heyday). ★1926: 'Original Oldenkott' PIPES advertised nationally in Berlin (OUR eu_ft find). 1929: buys the Ahaus + Neuss Hermann-Oldenkott factories. 1932: German company's own PIPE production begins (pipedia). Post-war: Germany's #2 pipe maker (after VAUEN). TURBO series (motor-block-turned, silver-grey lacquer — 'probably influenced Porsche Design'; actual Porsche Design pipes = Elbert Gubbels, pipephil). 1972: bought by NIEMEIJER (NL); 1974 tobacco production CEASES — pipes only. Lopes variant: Hallen factory closed April 1982, some workers -> VAUEN (vauen.json link). 1987: Kersten family buys the pipe company back; 1992: CLOSED. 2012: marks acquired by Alexander Strähnz (Cologne) -> Italian-made REVIVAL (smaller bowls, slimmer shanks; premium models get the historic RED+WHITE DOT mark back). 1973 catalog documented (qualities/shapes in mirror). 'Bruyere Prima' probably 1950s. Sub-brands: EMINENT, EXCELLENT, EXCELSIOR (+ horseshoe stamp — THE BARI TRAP RESOLVED: an 'Excellent' with horseshoe = Oldenkott, NOT Bari), MAXIM (for Terella/Wolsdorff; post-closure made by Design Berlin), OLDEX, MICHELLE VISCONTI (trademark registered 1981-06-23, DELETED 2002 = a clean window), Derby ('Derby by Oldenkott', horseshoe). 'Danish Design' stamped Eminent/Excellent = the 60s-70s Danish-wave era. ★EGRA ADDED 2026-08-01 (customer correction, verified): pipedia's Oldenkott model list carries 'Oldenkott Egra' between Dorado and Eminent (shape numbers NOT recorded there). NO source anywhere links EGRA to Hilson — 0 hits across pipephil's whole brand index, and Hilson's documented lines are Elan/Fantasia/Avanti/Bolero/Maestro/New Tone/Royal Club/Unicorn/Viva/Mastro. Confidence MEDIUM: one source, no corroborating shape number. ⚠️Ahaus is a TOWN in Westphalia, not a parent company — Oldenkott's own factory was there ('Herms, Oldenkott und Zonen in Ahaus', 1918 print; 1929 bought the Ahaus + Neuss Hermann-Oldenkott factories). EGRA therefore points to GERMANY, never Belgium.

brand_marks.physical: Horseshoe stamp on sub-brands (Excellent, Derby). Red+white stem dot = historic premium mark (revived 2012+). Turbo = ribbed motor-block bowl, silver-grey lacquer. 1973-catalog quality names (Supra, Rubin, Nicofry w/ ring, Privat...) + 1-3 digit shape numbers.
